claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 10,500 infantry and 800 cavalry, total 11,300; side B (Spanish) 19,000 infantry and 1,000 cavalry, total 20,000.
claims.rationale: Claim-relevant rendering of the contextual quote/table. Bodart’s rounded-up available-for-engagement convention is shared, not an opening muster. claims.value: Suchet gives side A fewer than 9,000 in 13 infantry battalions, seven cavalry squadrons and twelve guns before Robert’s arrival.
claims.rationale: Initial field subset, excluding detached Laval and not a post-arrival whole-army count. English rendering (ours): "With thirteen infantry battalions, seven cavalry squadrons and twelve guns, in all fewer than nine thousand men."

citations.locator: suchet-t1, printed p. 27, Internet Archive leaf 96; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: avec treize bataillons d’infanterie, sept escadrons de cavalerie, et douze pièces de canon, en tout moins de neuf mille hommes.

claims.value: Toreno gives side B at most 12,000 present at Maria, with Areizaga’s 5,000 still detached at Botorrita.
claims.rationale: Present and absent populations distinct; neither silently replaced by Bodart’s 20,000 available total. English rendering (ours): "The force present did not exceed 12,000; Areizaga’s division of 5,000 combatants remained detached at Botorrita."

citations.locator: toreno-t3, printed p. 29, Internet Archive leaf 34; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: La fuerza allí presente no pasaba de 12,000 hombres, continuando destacada en Botorrita la división de Areizaga compuesta de 5000 combatientes.

claims.value: Suchet orders Robert’s approaching regiments to Santa Fe without halting; Laval remains a detached covering command at Mont Torrero.
claims.rationale: The page names Robert immediately before the order and distinguishes Laval’s detached task; no simultaneous-presence assumption. English rendering (ours): "He ordered him to proceed without halting toward Santa Fe."

citations.locator: suchet-t1, printed p. 27, Internet Archive leaf 96; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: il lui envoya l’ordre de se porter, sans faire halte, vers le couvent de Santa-Fé.

claims.value: Toreno places Blake with Roca’s first line and Lazan over the second.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Roca commanded the first line and Blake remained there from the start; Lazan headed the second."

citations.locator: toreno-t3, printed p. 29, Internet Archive leaf 34; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: La primera de estas la mandaba Don Pedro Roca, y en ella se mantuvo desde el principio Don Joaquín Blake. Estaba al frente de la segunda el marqués de Lazan.

claims.value: Suchet describes a French attack order as the Spanish army itself moved to extend its left.
claims.rationale: Author qualifies Spanish intention as if; concurrent main movements, not an inferred motive. English rendering (ours): "At two the attack order was given; movement began across the line as the Spanish army itself moved, extending its left as if to outflank us."

citations.locator: suchet-t1, printed p. 28, Internet Archive leaf 97; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: A deux heures l’ordre d’attaquer fut donné. Le mouvement commença sur toute la ligne au moment où l’armée espagnole elle-même s’ébranlait, étendant sa gauche comme pour nous déborder.

claims.value: Suchet describes a ravine separating the armies, with Musnier ordered across.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "A ravine separated us; Musnier’s division was ordered to cross it."

citations.locator: suchet-t1, printed p. 28, Internet Archive leaf 97; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Un ravin nous séparait : la division Musnier eut ordre de le franchir
